A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RPG research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching derivations relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen2.5 training experiments, mathematical benchmark results in Table 3, and optimizer and clipping comparisons in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 reports original Qwen3-4B experiments in Tables 3 and 5, with clipping, KL-coefficient, and reference-update ablations in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The KL objectives, surrogate losses, and Algorithms 1–2 are retained; RPG-Style Clip largely foregrounds existing dual-clip machinery. However, v2 Remark D.2 additionally describes replacing w and log w with clipped versions inside stop-gradient, without reconciling this description with the retained gradient-stopping branches in Algorithm 2. Whether this represents a procedural change or inconsistent documentation is unclear.

E1.justification: Evaluation coverage narrows from AIME24, AIME25, AMC23, and appendix MATH500 experiments in v1 to AIME24 and AIME25 in v2. The English-filtered, 13.9k-sample DAPO-Math-17k training set remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates GRPO, DAPO, REINFORCE++, and REINFORCE++-Baseline. v2 retains only GRPO and DAPO in its benchmark comparisons. Normalized FKL/RKL RPG variants also disappear from empirical comparisons, although their formulations remain documented. GSPO is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Qwen3-4B replaces Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Math-7B, and the AdamW/Schedule-Free comparison becomes AdamW-only. Maximum training/rollout length changes from 16,384 to 4,096/8,192 tokens for the labeled 2K/4K settings. Default RPG-REINFORCE clipping changes from (0.1,0.1) to (0.2,0.28). v2 reports GRPO clipping inconsistently: (0.2,0.2) in Section 5 versus (0.1,0.1) in Appendix F.

E4.justification: v1's two-model, two-optimizer sensitivity suite and associated collapse examples are removed. v2 repeats the clipping-range comparison under Qwen3 settings and adds targeted experiments comparing beta=1e-3 versus 1e-4 and fixed versus iteratively updated reference policies (Appendix G, Figures 6–7). These substantially revise the questions and evidence examined.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and training curves without documented independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. v2's additional results do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: The Qwen2.5 result suite is replaced by Qwen3 results at two context settings and new ablation curves. For example, v1 Table 3 reports RPG-REINFORCE-FKL's AIME24 Best score of 0.1667; v2 Table 3 reports RPG-REINFORCE-URKL's AIME25 Last score of 0.4125 versus DAPO's 0.3510. These are different experiments, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The generalized policy-gradient result, four KL gradient/loss derivations, k3–UKL equivalence, and stop-gradient proofs retain their mathematical substance. Normalized results move to Appendices C–D. v2 Proposition 4.1 consolidates equivalences already established in v1, and its explicit corrected GRPO estimator restates the importance weighting described in v1 Section 2.2.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes a systematic derivation framework with competitive or improved performance against several baselines. v2 makes RPG-Style Clip and off-policy REINFORCE viability central contributions, claims clipping preserves RPG gradients, and foregrounds stable, scalable training with up to six percentage points over DAPO. The REINFORCE++ analysis is removed from the contribution list.

C2.justification: v1's explanations favor tighter clipping for Qwen2.5-Math and Schedule-Free averaging; Appendix I.5 also favors directly differentiable losses. v2 removes these discussions and develops clip-higher, response-length, entropy, and reference-update interpretations for its new experiments. Its claim that larger clipping improves performance by decreasing entropy conflicts with Figure 6, which shows higher entropy for the better-performing larger-clip settings.

D1.justification: v2 expands reference-update documentation with periodic or KL-threshold triggers, but supplies no values for K or kappa. Hyperparameter documentation is revised and Schedule-Free implementation discussion removed. The code link, verl/vLLM framework, cached old-policy probabilities, and eight-H100 hardware disclosure remain. Conflicting GRPO clipping values reduce reproducibility clarity.

R1.justification: v2 adds Qwen3 and GSPO references and a short positioning paragraph emphasizing off-policy weighting and estimator equivalence. It removes the Schedule-Free and MiniCPM/WSD references and the detailed REINFORCE++ critique. Most of the related-work survey remains unchanged; duplicate Qwen2.5 references are consolidated.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, experimental discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Normalized KL material moves into Appendices C–D, Section 4.1 becomes a clipping presentation, and the REINFORCE++ background subsection and optimizer discussion disappear. This materially reorganizes the narrative beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: The combined loss tables are reorganized into unnormalized main-text tables and a normalized appendix table. v1's Figure 5 moves into the main text as v2 Figure 2. Benchmark tables lose methods and columns, a separate 2K table appears, and the extensive six-panel experimental displays are replaced by five-panel comparisons and new ablation figures.

improvement.justification: v2 improves focus, adds useful KL-coefficient/reference-update ablations, and removes v1's erroneous AIME25 claim of 0.95729 where Table 3 actually gives 0.0573. However, it removes substantial benchmark, model, optimizer, and baseline evidence while strengthening scalability and gradient-preservation claims. Conflicting GRPO settings and the entropy explanation contradicted by Figure 6 introduce credibility costs. The gains in targeted analysis and clarity coexist with losses in evidential breadth and consistency, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
